provenance.prompt:
Create an original six-pose right-facing action sprite sheet for Paprika's JAMVERSE '96 `pass-overhead` basketball animation. Use the attached Paprika pass and shot sheets as the exact character identity and sprite-style references. Paprika is canonically a REAL TINY FOUR-FOOTED KIT FOX: horizontal fox body, russet-orange fur, cream-white muzzle/chest/underside, huge triangular ears, bright fox eyes, pointed muzzle, a large bushy tail with a pale tip, and her fitted purple-and-gold sports vest. Preserve her established natural small-fox proportions and all four animal legs. She must remain quadruped in every pose: never anthropomorphic, human-shaped, upright like a person, or equipped with hands, shoes, shorts, or a cloak.

Draw exactly 6 distinct, complete, independently redrawn full-body fox poses on a true transparent RGBA background, arranged in 3 columns by 2 rows in strict left-to-right, top-to-bottom order. Keep the same figure scale and a stable paw baseline. Leave generous empty transparent space around every figure and between every cell so the tall ears, muzzle, paws, and entire pale tail tip stay inside the cell; no clipping, touching, overlap, fused figures, cell outlines, grid lines, or panels. Match the crisp, colorful, richly shaded 1990s arcade pixel-sprite style and palette of the references. No basketball is drawn: gameplay renders and tracks the separate ball at Paprika's muzzle. No floor, shadow, court, hoop, opponent, extra person, prop, lettering, numerals, logos, glow, or background.

Pose sequence for a high lob pass using a natural fox nose-flick, never human arms: (0) gather low on all four paws, nose close to the invisible ball, alert eyes toward her teammate; (1) compress her hindquarters and brace both forepaws while drawing her neck and muzzle back; (2) push from her hind legs in a small bound as her chest rises, forepaws still visibly animal paws; (3) RELEASE anchor: sharply flick the pointed muzzle upward and forward toward the teammate, forepaws lifting naturally, mouth empty, no ball or other object; (4) follow through in a short airborne fox bound with muzzle reaching after the lob and bushy pale-tipped tail counterbalancing; (5) land forepaws then hind paws and recover on all fours, eyes tracking the pass. Every pose is different and anatomically plausible for the same small fox; do not repeat, warp, or duplicate any pose.

review.notes: Visual/source review confirms six distinct full-body right-facing kit-fox poses in 3x2 row-major cells, true RGBA transparency, no ball or props, four-legged fox anatomy in every pose, in-bounds ears/paws/tail, and the frame-3 nose-flick lob release. Six large alpha components are isolated from faint disconnected sheet artifacts; no figure is fused or excluded.

provenance.packaging: package-action6.py; 144x96 cells; baseline94; lossless WebP; 6 original pass-overhead poses
